'''Lonnie Lee Van Zandt''' (1937&ndash;1995) was a professor of [[physics]] at [[Purdue University]] in [[Indiana]], USA.

Van Zandt participated in the formation of the [[molecular biology|molecular biological]] physics group at Purdue and studied the dynamics of dissolved DNA [[polymers]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.cell.com/biophysj/retrieve/pii/S0006349594807313|title=Local Modes in a DNA Polymer with Hydrogen Bond Defect|last1=Saxena|first1=V.K.|last2=Van Zandt|first2=L.L.|journal=Biophysical Journal|volume=67|date=December 1994|pages=2448–2453|access-date=18 September 2020|publisher=The Biophysical Society}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1993SPIE.1890...13D|title=Dynamics of dissolved DNA polymers with counterions|last1=Dorfman|first1=Barry H.|last2=Saxena|first2=V.K.|last3=VanZandt|first3=Lonnie L.|journal=Proceedings of the SPIE|publisher=SPIE|date=May 1993|volume=1890|pages=13–23|doi=10.1117/12.145255|access-date=18 September 2020}}</ref> He also performed pioneering research on the effect of [[microwave]]s on [[DNA]].<ref>M. E. Davis and L. L. Van Zandt (1988) ''Microwave response of DNA in solution'' [[Physical Review]], Volume 37, Issue 3, pages 888–901 [http://pra.aps.org/abstract/PRA/v37/i3/p888_1]</ref> His PhD thesis in Physics at [[Harvard University]] focused on the "Effects of Static Spin Density Waves on Electron Transport".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.physics.harvard.edu/uploads/files/thesesPDF/PhD1954-1970.pdf |title=Harvard Physics Thesis |access-date=2014-05-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140518025727/https://www.physics.harvard.edu/uploads/files/thesesPDF/PhD1954-1970.pdf |archive-date=2014-05-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
